dynamicAuthz: observability_console:open for /grafana/ and /kiali/; database_console:open for pgAdmin and mongo-express; objectstore_console:open for the RustFS object store; sysadmin for any unrecognised path. Which one applies comes from the GATEWAY — the `X-PB-Console` header it states, or the `X-Original-URI` it forwards — so no single id can gate the route.

The same chain as the console check: observability_console:open, database_console:open or objectstore_console:open by the class the caller states in `X-PB-Console`, sysadmin for an unrecognised one, plus the system org and AAL2.

a SYSTEM-org member holding `impersonation:open` for any target (cross-tenant, and still subject to the target organisation's consent policy), or an admin/owner of a strict ancestor of the target's org holding `team_access:open` for its own subtree. Resolved per request against the org the session would pin to.
the superadmin FLAG only — no permission grants emergency access, because it bypasses the target organisation's consent policy. Approved by a SECOND superadmin (four-eyes).

ANY authenticated caller; the result set is filtered to what they may act on — their own requests as subject or requester, their org subtree as a tenant admin holding `impersonation:approve` (the to-decide view only; revocable sessions do not need it), and the break-glass queue for the superadmin FLAG. The old declaration named an authority gate this route does not have. Not `system-org`: holding `impersonation:open` adds nothing to this list beyond your own requests.

never the requester; then ORDINARY requests are decided by the named approver, or by an admin/owner of the target org (or an ancestor of it) holding `impersonation:approve` — a superadmin is REFUSED here on purpose, because consent belongs to the tenant. BREAK-GLASS requests are the opposite: a second superadmin and nobody else (four-eyes).

the REQUESTER only, with their authority re-resolved now rather than trusted from request time — so a lost permission, admin role or org relationship refuses the redemption. That means a parent-org admin too, not only the vendor: the previous declaration said "sysadmin", which was never the whole set. Break-glass redemption stays flag-only.

the subject, the requester, the decider, or an admin of the pinned org (`canAdministerOrg`, which a superadmin satisfies). Revoking only ever REMOVES access, so the set is wide deliberately — the previous declaration named only two of the four.
